text:
A: Hiya! Can you hear me okay? I'm never sure with this laptop, it sort of freezes if Rob's downloading anything.
B: Yes, I can hear you lovely! Hiya, I'm Rowena. You're Gemma, yeah?
A: That's me, yeah. Ooh, I love your glasses. Sorry, that's a weird way to start.
B: No, no, I'll take it! Nobody compliments me at work, they just bleep me. Where are you, then? Are you from round here, wherever here is?
A: Beeston, so just outside Nottingham. Born and bred, really. What about you?
B: Warrington. Great Sankey. But originally from the Philippines, Batangas, I came over in 2003 with the nurse recruitment. Twenty years now, so I'm basically Northern.
A: Oh, you're a nurse? I'm in pharmacy! I'm a pharmacy technician at the hospital in Nottingham.
B: No way! NHS! What do you do, the dispensary?
A: Dispensary mostly, erm, and then I go up on the wards for medicines reconciliation, so sort of checking what people are actually taking at home against what's written down. Which is never the same, do you know what I mean? Someone'll say "oh, I take the little white one" and you're like, right, okay, which little white one, there's about four hundred.
B: [laughs] The little white one! I get that with creams. "The one in the blue tube, love." I'm tissue viability, so pressure ulcers, wounds, that kind of thing.
A: Oh, that's a specialist job, isn't it?
B: Band 7, yeah. I love it, honestly. I do a lot of teaching for the healthcare assistants and the new nurses, and I try to make it fun, because pressure ulcers on a PowerPoint, you know, people's eyes go.
A: I do the training for our new starters! I've got colour-coded checklists, it's a bit of a joke in the department. They call me the highlighter lady.
B: Oh, you'd hate my inbox. It's a disaster. I'd rather go and see a patient than answer an email.
A: [laughs] Fair enough. Erm, sorry, I noticed in your photo, is that a choir rota on your board?
B: Yes! Filipino choir at my parish. We're practising for a fiesta at the minute. Do you sing?
A: I do! Church music group at the Methodist church, I'm an alto, and then a community choir that does pop stuff. We're learning a new one for a summer concert and I keep singing the soprano line by accident.
B: Ah, that's lovely. I knew it, I saw your cross and thought, she'll be a singer.
A: [laughs] That's very good detective work. Is it all hymns, yours, or...
B: Hymns on Sunday, then at the parties it's karaoke, Whitney, Celine. No mercy.
A: Oh, I'd be in tears. I cry at everything. I went to Les Mis at the Theatre Royal and Rob had to give me his sleeve.
B: Me and my work friends do the Palace in Manchester. We saw Wicked and I was a mess. Do you have kids, Gemma?
A: One, Isla, she's six. Dinosaurs and loom bands at the minute. My wrists are covered in them, I look like I've been to a festival.
B: [laughs] I'm the fun auntie. My sister's two, Mia's fifteen, Ethan's eleven. We all live together, it's chaos but nice chaos.
A: Aw, that sounds lovely, actually. My mum does two pick-ups a week for us, I'd be lost without her. Sorry, I'm rambling, aren't I?
B: No, I'm the same! We're going to get told off by the timer. What do you do on a Saturday, then? I always get a barm from the bakery, that's my treat.
A: A barm! See, we'd say cob. A cheese cob from the market.
B: Cob! That sounds like a horse.
A: [laughs] It's a perfectly good word, thank you very much!
